name: pyrite
description: Read Python as if it were Java: mirrors a Python project into a read-only, Java-flavored view for Java developers.

commands.title: Pyrite: Generate Java View for Workspace
Pyrite: Open Java View of This File

enumDescriptions: Deterministic rule-based translator. Fast, offline, no API key. Best-effort Java syntax.
Rules engine, plus a local Ollama model that rewrites only the functions the rules handle badly. Needs a running Ollama; falls back to the rules output if it is not reachable.
pyrite.engine.description: Translation engine used to produce the Java view.

pyrite.ollama.url.description: Base URL of the Ollama server used by the hybrid engine.

pyrite.ollama.model.description: Ollama model used by the hybrid engine (a name from `ollama list`).

pyrite.ollama.timeoutSeconds.description: Give up on one Ollama request after this many seconds and keep the rules translation.

pyrite.ollama.maxFunctionsPerFile.description: At most this many functions per file are sent to Ollama; the rest keep the rules translation.

pyrite.outputFolder.description: Folder (relative to the workspace root) where the mirrored Java view is written.

pyrite.watch.description: Re-translate a Python file automatically whenever it is saved.

enumDescriptions: Every class and method gets Javadoc, written from its name when it has no docstring.
Only classes and methods that have a Python docstring get Javadoc.
No Javadoc. Docstrings stay as plain comments.
pyrite.javadoc.markdownDescription:
How much Javadoc to generate in the Java view.

- **Always generate**: every class and method, written from its name when it has no docstring.
- **Generate where exists** (default): only classes and methods that have a Python docstring.
- **Never generate**: no Javadoc. Docstrings stay as plain comments.

pyrite.javadocTestCode.description: Document test code. When unchecked (default), test files (test_*.py, *_test.py, conftest.py, or anything under a test/tests folder) never get Javadoc. When checked, test code follows the same pyrite.javadoc rules as production code.

pyrite.lombok.description: Use Lombok-style annotations instead of spelling out boilerplate: a class whose __init__ only assigns its parameters to fields gets @AllArgsConstructor, a trivial __str__/__repr__ becomes @ToString, a trivial __eq__/__hash__ becomes @EqualsAndHashCode, a @property/@x.setter pair that just wraps a field becomes @Getter/@Setter on that field, and a dataclass-like class (@dataclass, NamedTuple, pydantic BaseModel, ...) becomes @Data. Methods that don't match these simple shapes are left spelled out.

pyrite.lineWidth.markdownDescription:
Maximum line length of the generated Java, in columns. Longer lines are wrapped the way IntelliJ IDEA and palantir-java-format do by default.

- A method signature or call that does not fit puts **one parameter per line**, indented 8 spaces.
- Long conditions break before `&&` and `||`, string concatenation before `+`, and call chains before each `.call()`.

Long string literals are never split. Use **0** to turn wrapping off.
